newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BHP gas pipeline has environment okay.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BHP gas pipeline has environment okay.

text.p: The New South Wales government said on Tuesday that a commission of inquiry had given environmental approval to the construction of a A$380 million underground gas pipeline linking the Bass Strait fields in Victoria with Sydney.

The 750 kilometre Eastern Gas Pipeline is a joint venture between Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and Vancouver-baed Westcoast Energy Inc. BHP is the partner in the Bass Strait oil and gas fields with Exxon Corp.
State premier Bob Carr said the government would now formally determine if the project should be approved.
Carr said the inquiry's findings would be assessed by NSW Planning Minister Craig Knowles who would then advise Energy Minister Michael Egan whether or not to okay the project.
He said the pipeline would create nearly 6,000 jobs and bring about A$250 million of direct investment into New South Wales.

"The pipeline is a jobs bonanza for NSW, and particularly for the Illawarra (region south of Sydney)," Carr said, with strict permit and licence conditions to be placed on the project dealing that dealt with environmental and social impacts of the pipeline.
In NSW, the pipeline will run north through Bombala, Cooma, Michelago, Hoskinstown, Nerriga, Nowra, Berry and Wollongong.
BHP said on June 18 that the project was scheduled to begin operations in 1997 or 1998, subject to government approval.
The pipeline would provide competition in the gas markets of Canberra, Sydney, Wollongong and Newcastle, BHP said.
